source_text: Ipsam postremo arbitrii libertatem unius peccati impulsione subrueret, ut nemo deinceps in potestate haberet vetera crimina virtutis electione respuere, sed uno omnes in condemnationem eversae humanitatis torrente raperentur.
pass_a_gloss: Finally he would undermine the very freedom of decision by the impulse of one sin, so that no one thereafter would have in his power to spit out old crimes by a choice of virtue, but all would be seized in one torrent of overturned humanity into condemnation.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS electio=choice; Blaise not later predestination 'election' unless forced

pass_b_english: —and finally overthrew the very freedom of the will by the impact of one sin, so that afterward no one had the power to reject former crimes by choosing virtue, but everyone was swept in a single torrent of ruined humanity toward condemnation—

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
